description:
Seen 2026-10-26 on 0.19.0 with Claude Code 2.1.310, in a pane started with `extras/claude-code/messaging-hooks.json`. Claude Code runs PostToolUse hooks for a subagent's tool calls too, and the hook's payload then carries `agent_id` and `agent_type` (logged: `{"agent_id":"a2390a287e6a1b7f5","agent_type":"general-purpose","tool_name":"Bash"}`). The read hook checks neither, so whichever context makes the next tool call takes the message body and marks it read.

Reproduced: the pane's agent started a background subagent that made a Bash call every 5 s, then ran a 40 s command in the foreground. A post arrived, and 6 s later the subagent's PostToolUse hook handed it the body. The pane's agent got only the Stop hook's notice ("1 new (#5) ... Read: muster msg read"), and its own `muster msg read --if-unread` then printed nothing. When the pane's agent is idle instead, its Stop wait usually wins, by about a second in one run.

a_2nSw5pbpW was a nested `claude -p` that inherits `$MUSTER_PANE`. This subagent runs inside the pane's own Claude Code process.

Possibly: have the PostToolUse hook exit 0 when its stdin payload has an `agent_id`, so only the session's main agent reads. For example `[ -n "$(jq -r '.agent_id // empty')" ] && exit 0` ahead of the read, or a test without jq that the snippet can count on.
title: Messaging hooks hand the pane's message to a subagent's tool call
